Hi Ava —

Thanks, and good to continue the thread. I put together a concise evidence packet and a short exception playbook summary attached. TL;DR below; see attachments for screenshots and the one‑page decision log template.

Measurement windows and aggregation
- We publish two canonical SLOs: availability (successful response within latency budget) and latency (p95 for interactive routes, p99 for batch/async).
- Measurement window is sliding 30‑day rolling window with daily rollups and weekly snapshots. Aggregation: per‑route streaming aggregation at 1s granularity; then rollups to 1m and 1h for dashboards.
- Sampling: we always instrument 100% of production inference traffic for counters and latency histograms. For long‑tail storage/aggregation cost reasons we retain full histograms for 14 days, aggregates for 90 days, and 1y of summary metrics.

Synthetic vs real traffic
- Synthetic probes run from our three probe regions every 60s and are used for external availability alerting and cross‑region validation.
- Reconciliation: we reconcile probe data against production telemetry daily and surface delta alerts when synthetic and real traffic diverge by >2x error rate. Reconciliation rules and thresholds are in the attached reconciliation matrix.

Customer visibility and access
- Customers get read‑only access to a curated Grafana dashboard (per‑account view) for the last 90 days plus exportable CSVs for request-level traces when permitted by contract.
- For Dedicated and Private customers we offer optional dashboard hosting inside the customer's VPC; access model is managed by their security admin and subject to an entitlement request process documented in the attachment.
- Audit evidence: we provide quarterly uptime attestations and can provide ad‑hoc, time‑bounded exports for procurement/technical audits via secure transfer.

Exception playbook (summary)
- Planned maintenance: minimum 72h notice for anything expected >5m impact to p95; standard maintenance windows are 02:00–05:00 PT.
- Emergency exceptions: incident owner (SRE) declares temporary measurement carveout only after stakeholder sync (SRE → CS → Customer lead) and records rationale in the decision log.
- Retention: exception decisions and forensic artifacts retained 3 years.

Hi Liam —

Short answers for the checklist:
1) PII and redaction: by default, any exported request‑level data is redacted at ingestion to remove raw user content fields. We retain request metadata (latency, response codes, model version, truncated request id) that is sufficient for forensic reconstruction. Raw text payloads are only available via an explicit, auditable legal/data request workflow and require agreement on scope and an encrypted transfer. That workflow is documented in the SLO evidence packet (section 4).

2) 72h notice: that is our contractual minimum for planned maintenance impacting customer‑facing latency/availability commitments. If a customer requires a longer notice window we can add that to the contract as an SLA supplement. For unplanned/emergency maintenance the playbook specifies immediate notification and post‑incident decision logging.
